title: Defining Average and Instantaneous Rates of Change at a Point
core_idea: Average rate compares total change over an interval, while instantaneous rate describes the limiting rate at one input.
what_students_need_to_understand: This is the bridge from limits to derivatives and appears whenever slope, velocity, or change at an instant is being interpreted.

title: Defining the Derivative of a Function and Using Derivative Notation
core_idea: The derivative is the limit of the difference quotient and represents instantaneous rate of change or tangent-line slope.
what_students_need_to_understand: Derivative notation becomes the language for nearly every later unit, including motion, optimization, differential equations, and accumulation.
how_this_becomes_points: You earn points by writing correct derivative notation, interpreting it in context, and connecting the derivative to a limit or slope.
answer_move: Translate f'(a) as the instantaneous rate of change of f with respect to x at x = a.

title: Connecting Differentiability and Continuity
core_idea: Differentiability at a point means a derivative exists there, and differentiability implies continuity at that point.
what_students_need_to_understand: This topic prevents invalid derivative claims at corners, cusps, vertical tangents, jumps, and holes.
how_this_becomes_points: You earn points by checking whether the function is continuous and whether the local slope behavior has one consistent finite value.
answer_move: Use the chain: differentiable -> continuous. If continuity fails, differentiability fails too.
mini_example_question: A calculus prompt asks you to justify a conclusion involving Connecting Differentiability and Continuity. What should your work and sentence make clear?
weak_answer: I would write the final value or conclusion without showing why it follows.
point_attaining_answer: Use the chain: differentiable -> continuous. If continuity fails, differentiability fails too. Then make the scoring connection explicit: You earn points by checking whether the function is continuous and whether the local slope behavior has one consistent finite value.
common_point_loss: Claiming a derivative exists at a corner or discontinuity because the graph has points on both sides.

title: Applying the Power Rule
core_idea: The power rule differentiates x^n by multiplying by the exponent and reducing the exponent by one.
what_students_need_to_understand: It is the most common derivative tool and supports later work with motion, optimization, and graph analysis.
how_this_becomes_points: You earn points by applying the exponent change accurately, including negative and fractional powers after rewriting radicals or reciprocals.
answer_move: Rewrite the expression as powers of x first, then apply d/dx x^n = n x^(n-1).

weak_answer: I would write the final value or conclusion without showing why it follows.
point_attaining_answer: Rewrite the expression as powers of x first, then apply d/dx x^n = n x^(n-1). Then make the scoring connection explicit: You earn points by applying the exponent change accurately, including negative and fractional powers after rewriting radicals or reciprocals.
common_point_loss: Dropping coefficients or mishandling negative and fractional exponents.

title: The Product Rule
core_idea: The product rule differentiates a product by differentiating each factor once while leaving the other factor unchanged.
what_students_need_to_understand: Many AP expressions are products designed to test whether students choose structure-aware differentiation instead of distributing or guessing.
how_this_becomes_points: You earn points by showing both product-rule terms and applying any needed inner derivative inside each factor.
answer_move: Write first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first before simplifying.

weak_answer: I would write the final value or conclusion without showing why it follows.
point_attaining_answer: Write first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first before simplifying. Then make the scoring connection explicit: You earn points by showing both product-rule terms and applying any needed inner derivative inside each factor.
common_point_loss: Differentiating both factors at once or omitting one of the two product-rule terms.

title: The Quotient Rule
core_idea: The quotient rule differentiates a ratio by combining the derivative of the numerator and denominator over the denominator squared.
what_students_need_to_understand: It is a frequent source of sign and order errors, especially when quotient structure is nested inside applied questions.
how_this_becomes_points: You earn points by preserving the quotient-rule order, squaring the denominator, and simplifying only after the derivative structure is correct.
answer_move: Use low d-high minus high d-low over low squared, then check signs before simplifying.
